subject: Environment
description: Myers' criteria, India's 4 hotspots, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Himalaya, Sundaland

questions.stem: The term 'biodiversity hotspot' was introduced in 1988 by:
questions.explanation: British ecologist Norman Myers first proposed the 'hotspot' concept in the journal Environmentalist (1988). Conservation International later formalised two criteria — (1) contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics (>0.5% of the world's total), and (2) have lost at least 70% of its primary native vegetation. As of 2026, 36 hotspots are recognised globally.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: How many biodiversity hotspots are recognised in India as of 2026?
questions.explanation: India hosts parts of 4 global biodiversity hotspots: (1) the Himalaya, (2) Indo-Burma, (3) Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and (4) Sundaland (covering only the Nicobar group in India). Together they cover ~2% of India's area but harbour a huge share of its endemic species. The Andaman Islands are NOT formally part of Sundaland; only the Nicobars are.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Western Ghats — a UNESCO World Heritage site — is shared by how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: Western Ghats runs through 6 states along India's west coast: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu. Declared a UNESCO WHS in 2012 (39 sub-sites). It pre-dates the Himalayas geologically — 150 million years old. Hosts endemic species — Lion-tailed macaque, Malabar civet, Nilgiri tahr, purple frog. Gadgil Committee (2011) and Kasturirangan Committee (2013) proposed ecosensitive zoning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the two criteria Conservation International uses to identify a biodiversity hotspot?

options.option_text: At least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species
At least 70% of primary native vegetation lost
Presence of at least one endemic mammal species

questions.explanation: The two-criterion test is based ONLY on vascular plant endemism + habitat loss. Mammals / birds are not required. The logic: plant diversity is the foundation of ecosystem services, and if you protect endemic-plant-rich landscapes you automatically protect most associated fauna. Many hotspots (e.g. Madagascar, New Caledonia) happen to have unique mammals, but that's a by-product, not a qualifying criterion.

questions.stem: The Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot in India includes:

options.option_text: All of North-East India except Assam plains, plus parts of West Bengal

questions.explanation: Indo-Burma hotspot covers much of mainland Southeast Asia, extending into India's NE hill states (Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya), southern Assam hills and northern WB. The Assam valley floor and the Eastern Himalayan foothills are part of the separate Himalaya hotspot. Indo-Burma is famous for freshwater turtles (world's highest diversity) and primate species.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Himalaya biodiversity hotspot is home to which iconic endangered cat found above the treeline?
questions.explanation: Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) inhabits the alpine zone (3,000-5,500 m) of the Himalayas — J&K, Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal. Project Snow Leopard launched 2009; SECURE Himalaya is the current UNDP-supported programme. Clouded leopards live in dense lower-elevation forests; leopard cat and fishing cat prefer lowlands. Snow leopard IUCN — Vulnerable (downlisted from Endangered in 2017).

questions.stem: 'Megadiverse countries' is a separate list of nations housing the majority of Earth's species. How many countries are on this list, and is India one of them?
questions.explanation: The Megadiverse Countries list — curated by UNEP-WCMC (1998) — includes 17 countries that together harbour >70% of Earth's species. India is on it, alongside Australia, Brazil, China, Colombia, DRC, Ecuador, Indonesia, Madagascar, Malaysia, Mexico, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Philippines, South Africa, USA, Venezuela. Don't confuse this with 'biodiversity hotspots' (36 — Myers/CI concept) — the criteria are different.
